findings.text: LOCUS_DEFINITION_CHECK's significance reads the second-height defect as gone for the node, but the record's own after-state shows radial_separatrix_distance_at_outboard_midplane still carrying the pre-merge locus sentence ('The data's midplane identifier selects that height, or it is the magnetic-axis height when none is given'); radial's documentation was generated 2026-10-20 under run_id b5eb53cc and never regenerated after the registry was merged, so the fragment's headline that both names were accepted after the locus registry stopped naming a second height holds for gap_at_outboard_midplane only. The record states the divergence nowhere, so the read is left to the reader.

DD_FIELD_RE matches only the underscore spelling \bmidplane_identifier\b, so radial's accepted documentation naming the same DD field in prose ('The data's midplane identifier selects that height') is reported as names_dd_field_or_path: false; the read-back check is narrower than the property the record and the fragment state, and whether a prose reference counts as naming a DD field is a judgement neither records.

report() writes the record from a live-graph read and the gate prints read_checks without asserting them, so the gate cannot fail on a graph drift or on a false read-back: it silently rewrites the record instead, and the gate log records only its own EXIT=0 line, leaving nothing that reddens if the recorded claims regress.

the invocation block attributes gap's regenerated documentation to docs_model=openrouter/openai/gpt-6-luna, while the record's own live read at shc-gap-docs-regen.json after.gap_at_outboard_midplane reports docs_model openrouter/openai/gpt-6.1-sol for the same name; the two may describe different regenerations, but the fragment never reconciles them and a reader cannot tell which seat produced the accepted text.
